hypothesis: Age Up (delta score): sites in the top fifth of the CHANGE in AP-1 binding score with age carry better AP-1 cores.
test: Exact TGA[C/G]TCA core, matched pairs, genome-wide scan of mm10
result: 84.5% of Age Up (delta score) sites vs 78.6% of matched Unchanged have an exact core (McNemar p = 0.02); mean difference in mismatch count -0.055 (p = 0.027).
detail: Earlier evidence was 78 scanned sites (90% vs 77%); this is the whole set.

hypothesis: Age Down (delta score): the same holds for sites LOSING binding score, i.e. it is about change, not direction.
result: 75.0% of Age Down (delta score) sites vs 75.5% of matched Unchanged (McNemar p = 0.93).
detail: If this were significant too, the H1 result would be about lability, not gain.

hypothesis: Dynamic (threshold): sites whose binding CALL changes in any condition carry worse AP-1 cores than context-matched Stable sites.
result: 74.4% vs 79.6% have an exact core (McNemar p = 0.065).
detail: Tests whether the threshold classes have a sequence signature of their own.

hypothesis: Where a MEF2 motif exists in the DNA, it is less often OCCUPIED at Dynamic sites (not merely less often detected).
test: MEF2 footprint called, among sites with a MEF2 consensus match within 100 bp and measured accessibility above the median; matched pairs
result: 100.0% of Dynamic vs 100.0% of matched Stable carry a MEF2 footprint (McNemar p = nan); over all motif-bearing sites 66.7% vs 100.0% (p = 1).
detail: Restricting to signal-rich sites removes most of the detection bias; a surviving deficit points to occupancy.

hypothesis: A condition-variable (threshold) AP-1 site sits beside a MEF2 footprint that is itself condition-variable, i.e. they are co-regulated.
test: Among AP-1 sites with a MEF2 footprint within 100 bp: is MEF2 condition-variable more often when AP-1 is? (Fisher); and do the two share the exact YS/MAS/MAE pattern more than chance (permutation)?
result: MEF2 is condition-variable at 67.7% of condition-variable AP-1 sites vs 5.5% of constitutive ones (OR 35.99, p = 4.2e-56); identical three-condition pattern in 87.8% of loci vs 74.5% expected (p = 0.002).
detail: Co-variation across conditions cannot be produced by a static detection bias. RETRACTED by H4b: every family in the peak co-varies with AP-1 about equally, so this is peak-level signal, not co-regulation.

hypothesis: Dynamic (threshold) sites sit among more AP-1 motifs, so no single one is essential.
test: Consensus TGA[C/G]TCA matches within 100 bp (sequence), matched pairs
result: median 3.0 vs 4.0 matches, mean difference -0.41 (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.014).
detail: A significant difference in the opposite direction counts as contradicted, not merely unsupported.

hypothesis: Control: AlphaGenome's motif dependence tracks the quality of the AP-1 core in the DNA.
test: Effect of replacing the motif, exact core vs not; and correlation with mismatch count
result: exact core -0.78 vs imperfect -0.10 log2 (p = 2.8e-89); rho with mismatches +0.331 (p = 9.9e-95).
detail: If this failed, the sequence scan and the model would be measuring different things.

hypothesis: The extra motif sensitivity of Age Up (delta score) sites is explained by their better cores (core quality is the mechanism, not a correlate).
test: Repeat the Age Up vs Unchanged matched comparison on the four motif-level edits, with and without core mismatch count added to the matching
result: significant motif edits: 0 of 4 matching on context only, 0 of 4 after also matching on core quality.
detail: A drop to zero means core quality carries the effect; no change means the two are separate.

hypothesis: The AP-1/MEF2 co-variation is SPECIFIC to MEF2, rather than every factor in the peak moving together.
test: Concordance of the three-condition pattern between AP-1 and each neighbouring family, MEF2 against the others
result: MEF2 agrees with AP-1 at 87.8% of loci; other families 80.6% to 88.9% (KLF/SP 85.6%, other 86.9%). When AP-1 is condition-variable, the neighbouring factor is too in 68% of MEF2 cases and 60% on average for the others.
detail: If every family agrees with AP-1 equally, the co-variation is peak-level signal, not co-regulation.

hypothesis: The extra motif sensitivity of Age Up (delta score) sites is robust to matching on MEASURED accessibility, not only predicted.
test: Age Up vs Unchanged on four motif-level edits, matched on 4 predicted-context variables vs the same plus measured accessibility
result: significant motif edits: 4 of 4 with predicted context only, 0 of 4 once measured accessibility is matched too.
detail: Measured accessibility is partly a consequence of the binding change being studied, so matching on it may be over-adjustment; this records the sensitivity either way.

hypothesis: The AP-1 sites that do not respond to destroying their motif are the ones without a perfect core.
test: Non-responder (replacing the motif changes accessibility by less than 10%) vs exact core, all sites
result: 53% of sites with an imperfect core are non-responders vs 21% with a perfect core (odds ratio 4.3, p = 2.4e-66); imperfect cores are 21% of sites and 41% of all non-responders.
